text.brief: Nine days before the midterm election of November 3, 2026, a volunteer for a House candidate in Michigan finds a local news site she has never heard of. It runs three stories on her candidate's votes on Taiwan, and each byline traces to no living reporter.
text.record: OpenAI reported on June 10, 2026 that two operations linked to the People's Republic used its models to push content on American data centers and tariffs ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/prc-linked-influence-operations-ai-debates/)). Microsoft reported in October 2024 that a mainland operation targeted down-ballot candidates who criticized the Party ([NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2024-election/chinese-influence-operation-targets-us-down-ballot-races-rcna176960)). The Justice Department disbanded the FBI's Foreign Influence Task Force in February 2025 ([Attorney General memorandum, February 5, 2025](https://www.justice.gov/ag/media/1388541/dl)).
text.reading: The Party does not pick an American side. It feeds each side the grievance it already holds, from electricity prices to tariffs, and aims its sharpest content at candidates who back Taiwan. Synthetic local news sites launder the message so that it arrives with a hometown masthead. This is Stratagem 33, sow discord among the enemy.
text.coreEvent: Operators linked to the Party target at least one 2026 congressional candidate with synthetic local news.
text.gapText: Application Architecture. Platforms label state media accounts but not the synthetic local sites that launder the same content.
text.fix: Label content by origin at the domain level and publish takedowns of foreign inauthentic networks. Nothing polices citizens' lawful speech.
